newsitem.title: USA: Thorn Apple processed meats profitable.
newsitem.headline: Thorn Apple processed meats profitable.

text.p: Thorn Apple Valley Inc, a meat and poultry processor, said Wednesday its processed meats operation was profitable in the fiscal first quarter compared with an operating loss a year ago.
"We have upgraded our product mix, fully implemented our new distribution network, and improved production performance at all our facilities," Joel Dorfman, president, said.
However, industry-wide fresh pork margins remain depressed, and the improved operating efficiencies at the Frederick fresh pork division only served to reduce losses in this operation, he added.
Earlier, Thorn Apple reported a loss for the first quarter ended September 20 of $0.29 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.89.

Processed meat sales volume was down about 15 percent, reflecting the company's focus on establishing and maintaining sufficient margins and product mix to return the processed meats operation to profitability.

"The lower volume has resulted in increased unit overhead costs; however, we have retained capacity in most product lines with the expectation that we will begin increasing our volumes from current levels," Dorfman said.
Sales commitments for ham products for the upcoming holiday season were very strong, and the company expected to utilize fully its ham capacity through December.
"We are developing various marketing programs to sustain our sales momentum in 1997," Dorfman said.

In fresh pork, hog slaughter volume was up about two percent, despite a four percent drop in hog supply for the period. The loss in the fresh pork division was significantly reduced from last year as the company began attaining targeted yield improvements from the Frederick slaughter plant.
According to the company, industry capacity in excess of available hog supplies continued to negatively affect hog margins as slaughterers bid up the price of hogs.

"Over the next few months, the negative imbalance between the industry's capacity and total hog production is expected to continue, and our financial improvement will likely be limited to gains in operating efficiencies," Dorfman said. "In the longer run, we are hopeful that the high prices recently paid for livestock will encourage producers to expand production, which historically improves fresh pork margins." He said the improved performance in processed meats is expected to continue.
